$comment: One fault per file. 'stage' is where the fault must be caught: 'parse' = the text is not YAML/JSON; 'structure' = it parses but violates the OpenAPI document structure; 'resolve' = a $ref cannot be resolved; 'semantic' = structurally valid but still wrong. 'pointer' is the JSON Pointer of the offending node, or of the parent when the fault is a missing key; null means no pointer is asserted. 'code', 'severity' and 'fatal' are from ADR 0004 'Fatal and degrading faults' (its table of the code each of the 16 must produce) and 'The M1 rule table' (severities). A fatal fixture gives buildModel model: null and exactly this finding with severity 'error' (criterion 5); every other fixture builds with this finding as a warning at this pointer, among others (criterion 6). The test asserts that a finding with this code is at this pointer, not that it is the only one, since the eleven that build declare no server or security scheme. A parse fault has pointer '' and its place in start and end (ADR 0004); for invalid-yaml and invalid-json the place is not asserted.

missing-paths-3.0.yaml.fault: required field 'paths' missing (3.0 only; legal in 3.1)

missing-responses-3.0.yaml.fault: required field 'responses' missing on an operation (3.0 only; legal in 3.1)

wrong-type-paths.yaml.fault: 'paths' is an array, expected an object

wrong-type-info-version.yaml.fault: 'info.version' is a number, expected a string

wrong-type-parameters.yaml.fault: 'parameters' is an object, expected an array

circular-ref.yaml.fault: A -> B -> A is a pure $ref cycle that never reaches a schema (not the same as a legal recursive schema)

external-ref.yaml.fault: $ref points at a remote URL; the engine has no I/O and must report it, not fetch it

duplicate-operation-id.yaml.fault: operationId 'ping' is used by two operations
